title: Gundam Launches First New Universe in Nearly 50 Years With 'Ghost in the Shell' Creator
excerpt: Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO unveils a brand-new timeline at San Diego Comic-Con, with SOLA Animation producing and a companion video game arriving in 2027.
body:
• Bandai Namco unveiled Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, marking the franchise's first entirely new timeline since its 1979 debut.
  • Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex director Kenji Kamiyama is writing and directing the series, with sci-fi novelist Toh EnJoe co-creating the story.
  • SOLA Animation, the studio behind The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, is producing the anime in partnership with Bandai Namco for a 2027 release.
  • A companion video game, Gundam Rogue Orbit, launches alongside on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.

For the first time in nearly half a century, the Gundam franchise is building a universe from scratch. Bandai Namco revealed Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO at San Diego Comic-Con 2026 on Thursday, announcing a brand-new anime series set in a timeline completely separate from the franchise's existing continuity. The series is set for a 2027 release.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=b6YBXoFAs3s

A New Timeline Built From the Ground Up

Since Yoshiyuki Tomino's original Mobile Suit Gundam premiered in 1979, the franchise has sprawled across dozens of series, films, and spin-offs — most of them set within established timelines like the Universal Century, Cosmic Era, or the more recent Ad Stella. XARX-ZERO represents something different: a clean break.

The new timeline, designated "After Apocalypse," is set 45 years after an alien object delivered three transformative technologies to humanity — gravity control, faster-than-light communication, and cognitive materialization — only to turn hostile, spawning a catastrophic ecosystem that forced humans to abandon Earth. The story follows Ray Azumi, a war orphan raised on the Moon who has never known life without the Apocalypse.

"I had been given the chance to create my own Gundam from the ground up for a series I've loved for years. What could be more exciting than that? Once I found my way back to that excitement, a fresh and unexpected Gundam began to take shape."

— Kenji Kamiyama, writer and series director

The Creative Team Behind the Project

Kenji Kamiyama, best known for directing Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex and The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, serves as writer and series director. He is joined by novelist and screenwriter Toh EnJoe, whose recent credits include Godzilla Singular Point and the 2026 Prime Video remake of The Ghost in the Shell.

SOLA Animation, the studio behind Joker: Laugh Riot, Lazarus, and War of the Rohirrim, is producing the anime. Japanese voice actor Takeo Otsuka, recognized for his roles as Jinshi in The Apothecary Diaries and Aquamarine Hoshino in Oshi no Ko, will voice protagonist Ray Azumi.

A Multimedia Push for the 50th Anniversary

XARX-ZERO is part of a larger multimedia initiative Bandai Namco is calling the "RG Project." Alongside the anime, a new action game titled Gundam Rogue Orbit will launch in 2027 on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam. The game, previously announced at IGN's Summer of Gaming 2026, features a new pilot and mobile suit in its own storyline.

A live-action Gundam film starring Sydney Sweeney for Netflix has also recently finished filming, adding to a franchise push timed around the 50th anniversary of the original series.

Why It Matters for Anime Fans Worldwide

Gundam has long been one of anime's most commercially significant franchises, generating billions in merchandise revenue through its model kit (Gunpla) line alone. For the global anime community — including a substantial fanbase across India and the broader South Asian diaspora — a fresh timeline removes the intimidation factor of decades of accumulated lore, offering a clean entry point to the franchise.

The combination of Kamiyama's track record in sophisticated sci-fi storytelling and SOLA's rising profile in international animation production positions XARX-ZERO as one of the most anticipated anime announcements of the year. Whether it can match the cultural footprint of the original Universal Century remains to be seen, but Bandai Namco is betting big that the answer is yes.
